analyzedSources.bodySummary: Maps roughness to several possible contexts and directs readers to a dermatologist when rough patches persist or do not respond to basic care.
Lists acne history, dead-cell build-up, genetics, sun damage and pollution as possible contributors while also covering professional procedures.
Uses beginner and barrier language but promotes a proprietary product path, which the MyMirror page intentionally avoids.
Describes textured skin with bumps, roughness and enlarged-looking pores and attributes it to a range of environmental and internal factors.
Connects dry-feeling skin with roughness and texture while presenting texture choice as a comfort and skin-type consideration.
Links scaly-looking skin with dryness and seasonal context, and advises professional help for persistent discomfort or colour and texture changes.
Uses India climate examples and recognisable roughness descriptions but makes broad cause claims and product-led recommendations.
Defines uneven texture as bumpy or rough and discusses congestion, but overstates environmental explanations and specific treatment conclusions.
Frames texture through exfoliation, hydration and protection, then moves rapidly into product recommendations and perfect-skin promises.
Groups texture causes and separates at-home from professional care, illustrating readers’ desire for a way to decide which path applies.

gaps: Many bundle distinct textures into one remedy.
differentiationOpportunities: Define texture as a visible clue.
Use observation and escalation guidance first.

judgmentChecks.notes: Ten direct pages were read; claims have been narrowed to what a reader can observe.
